title: [Decision] Under the `single` posture, does an organization-scoped audit-ledger reader also read deployment-level ledger rows, or are those for the platform administrator only?
body:
Ruled: 6457448424 · letter A · 2026-10-28T00:39Z

**One-line question:** In a single-organization deployment, when a customer gives an auditor (not a platform administrator) the right to read the whole compliance ledger, should that auditor also see the history of deployment-wide configuration changes (settings and other deployment-level state), or only the history of the organization's business records?

Filing gate: **③ maintainer-directed** — the maintainer, in the 18.2.0 wave-2 PM session (2026-10-27), verbatim: 「组织级审计权限能不能看到部署级的行 应该立决裁卡」. Raised by the os-dev report on the security card #26640 (open question 1). The security detail that led here stays withheld on #26640; this card asks only the scope question, which no longer carries key material on new writes (#26683, merged) and whose at-rest residue is #26687.

## Background

The ledger has no organization column (ADR-0131 D7). Its writers stamp the organization a row is about in `tenant_id`; rows about deployment-level objects (objects with no organization column) carry `tenant_id` NULL. The read-all capability lifts the parent-record read gate only; the row scope comes from the platform row policy `sys_audit_log_org` (`tenant_id == current_user.organization_id`) in plugin-security's default sets.

## Governing text

- `packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts:81`, the capability description: "Under an organization wall an organization reader's row scope is the rows about its organization (tenant_id); a platform administrator reads every row, deployment-level rows included." — it states the walled postures and the platform administrator; it says nothing about `single`.
- `packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts:70-80` (comment): "under a wall-enforcing tenancy posture the platform row policy on that field (`sys_audit_log_org` …) still bounds a holder to its own organization's rows … A platform administrator reaches every row, deployment-level rows included, through its superuser read bypass, not through this capability."
- ADR-0131 point 2–3: "In a single-tenant deployment the organization *is* the environment"; "A table with no organization column is deployment-level or code-level, governed by permission, not by a wall."

Protocol: no published schema shape changes under either option; option C changes a capability's published description text (spec), option A changes runtime read behaviour.

## Premise (re-check)

- `git grep -n "sys_audit_log_org" packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts` → the policy is `tenant_id == current_user.organization_id`, so under a wall a NULL-tenant row is never in an organization reader's scope.
- Under `single` there is no wall, so that bound does not apply, and an organization-scoped holder's scope is every row its ledger grant reaches, deployment-level rows included (measured on #26640, detail withheld). NOT measured under `group` / `isolated` with a custom set that omits the default row policy — the execution step below measures it first.

## Options

| Option | What it does | What the customer sees | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | One rule in every posture: deployment-level ledger rows (`tenant_id` NULL) are served only to the platform administrator (or a separately named platform capability); an organization-scoped holder reads only rows about its organization(s). | A single-org auditor no longer sees deployment configuration history; the platform administrator still does. Walled postures unchanged. | server lane · 1 PR (`audit-log-read-visibility.ts` + pins + capability text sentence). No same-size precedent; nearest is #22266 (+1065/−257), which built the row scope itself. |
| **C** | Keep the behaviour; amend the capability text to say that under `single` the organization scope includes deployment-level rows, because there the organization is the environment. | Nothing changes at runtime; the documented scope finally covers `single`. | spec lane · 1 PR (text only). No measured precedent. |

(Option B from the dev report — stamping deployment-level rows with the default organization under `single` — is not offered: it re-attributes history and reverses ADR-0131 D7's meaning of deployment-level.)

## Business meaning

- **A** = the "data audit" vs "setup audit" split most platforms make: reading what happened to records is one right; reading what happened to the system's configuration is an administrator's right (Salesforce: Setup Audit Trail needs "View Setup and Configuration"; ServiceNow: configuration audit is admin-gated).
- **C** = in a one-company deployment the company is the system, so its auditor sees everything the ledger holds, as one auditor does in a small on-prem install.

## Four axes (business stance)

① Long-term: A makes the three postures behave the same (deployment rows are never an organization's), shrinking a posture-specific exception; C writes a posture difference into the capability's contract and keeps it forever.
② Business pull today: the auditor role is a custom grant (held by default only by platform administrators), so few stock deployments reach it; under C nothing breaks; under A a customer who built such an auditor on `single` loses configuration history visibility.
③ Anti-AI-error / failure mode: under C, a wrong grant fails silently (an auditor sees configuration history nobody intended); under A, it fails loudly (the auditor sees fewer rows and asks).
④ Startup non-sprawl: C costs one sentence; A costs one read rule and its pins, but no new key or declared surface.

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
os-decision-facets
- ① 项目长远合理性:A 让三种部署形态同一规则(部署级行永不属于组织),缩小特例;C 把形态差异写进权限契约,永久保留。
- ② 实际业务拉动:该能力默认只有平台管理员持有,自建审计员角色的 single 部署才会碰到;今天拉动小。
- ③ 防 AI 犯错:C 下授错权是静默多看;A 下是响亮少看。
- ④ 创业阶段不扩散:C 只改一句文字;A 加一条读规则与测试,不新增可声明键。

Prior rulings read: "audit log capability organization reader row scope deployment-level rows platform administrator tenant_id NULL" → 35 hits (none rules this question; #15207 / ADR-0131 D7 set the column model; #24164 is a different boundary); ADR-0131 D7; thread: none

## Recommendation

**A.** Only by ①: in two years the platform's ledger read model should be one rule across postures, with configuration history behind an administrator-level right, as the mainstream platforms model it; C freezes a `single`-only exception into a published contract. Confidence gap: not measured whether any shipped example or customer relies on a non-admin auditor reading configuration history under `single`.
Self-check: only ① gives A; do ②③④ flip it — no (② is small, ③ favours A, ④ favours C on cost but not enough to flip a contract question).
Not C: it documents the gap instead of closing it. Not B: see above.

## After the ruling

- **A:** dispatch one server-lane card: first measure `group` / `isolated` with a custom set lacking the default row policy (if NULL-tenant rows reach an organization holder there, that is a defect fixed in the same PR); then add the read rule in `audit-log-read-visibility.ts` (NULL-tenant rows only to the platform administrator), pins for each posture, and one sentence in the capability description; changeset + upgrade note for `single` operators who granted the capability.
- **C:** dispatch one spec-lane card for the capability description sentence and the docs page that restates it.

Related: #26640 (withheld), #26683, #26687, #15207, #22266.
